person.name: Jolene Marrowfield
person.target_direction: ICU charge / relief charge leadership, or a move into clinical informatics

roles.title: Registered Nurse, Medical ICU (Relief Charge Nurse since 2021)
roles.context: 24-bed Medical ICU in a 410-bed Level II trauma center; typical assignment 1:2, 1:1 for CRRT or unstable patients; 12-hour nights until 2020, days since. Relief charge about 6 shifts per month since March 2021.

accomplishments.title: CLABSI prevention bundle champion
accomplishments.problem: The MICU had 4 central line-associated bloodstream infections in calendar 2019, above the hospital's NHSN-benchmarked target, and bundle compliance audits were inconsistent.
accomplishments.actions: Volunteered as unit CLABSI champion in Jan 2020; built a daily line-maintenance audit checklist with the infection preventionist, did peer audits of dressing changes and CHG bathing on her shifts, and ran 10-minute huddle refreshers on scrub-the-hub and dressing integrity.
accomplishments.results: Bundle audit compliance rose from 71% to 96% over 6 months; the unit went 14 consecutive months with zero CLABSIs (Mar 2020 - Apr 2021).

accomplishments.title: Bedside shift report redesign
accomplishments.problem: Night-to-day handoff dragged on and nurses were clocking out late; key items (drips, lines, code status) were sometimes missed.
accomplishments.actions: Co-led a unit practice council workgroup that adopted an ICU-specific SBAR handoff sheet built into an Epic smartphrase, and piloted it on nights.
accomplishments.results: She recalls handoff used to take about 45 minutes per shift change and now takes about 25, twice a day. She has no formal measurement; it is her estimate and that of the council.

accomplishments.title: Relief charge nurse for 24-bed MICU
accomplishments.problem: Unit needed additional experienced nurses able to run the floor on shifts without a permanent charge nurse.
accomplishments.actions: Takes relief charge about 6 shifts a month: makes patient assignments for 10-12 RNs and 2 PCTs, manages bed flow with the house supervisor, responds to rapid responses and codes as a team member, handles staffing calls.
accomplishments.results: Has run the unit as charge on roughly 300 shifts since 2021 (6/month x ~4.5 yrs ~ 320; she says 'about 300').

accomplishments.title: Preceptor for new-graduate and transfer nurses
accomplishments.problem: High turnover after 2020 meant many new graduates entering the ICU via the nurse residency program.
accomplishments.actions: Precepted new RNs through the 12-week ICU orientation, using the unit competency checklist; co-taught the CRRT skills station at the annual competency fair.
accomplishments.results: Precepted 9 nurses since 2019 (6 new grads, 3 experienced transfers); 8 of the 9 completed orientation and were still on the unit at 1 year.

accomplishments.title: Epic ClinDoc super user during flowsheet upgrade
accomplishments.problem: 2022 Epic upgrade changed ICU flowsheets (drips, I&O, ventilator rows) and staff were frustrated with documentation time.
accomplishments.actions: Served as unit super user: attended 16 hours of super-user training, provided at-the-elbow support during go-live week, collected issues and sent 20+ build tickets to the informatics team, and created a one-page tip sheet for titratable drip documentation.
accomplishments.results: Informatics adopted her drip tip sheet house-wide for all 3 ICUs. No metric on documentation time.

accomplishments.title: CRRT super user
accomplishments.problem: Few nurses were comfortable running continuous renal replacement therapy, causing assignment bottlenecks.
accomplishments.actions: Became one of the unit's CRRT super users (Prismaflex), troubleshoots filter clotting and alarms, and co-teaches the annual competency station.
accomplishments.results: Qualitative: the go-to resource for CRRT on her shifts; no numbers on filter life were tracked.

roles.title: Registered Nurse, Medical-Surgical / Telemetry
roles.context: 32-bed med-surg/telemetry unit in a 180-bed community hospital; 5-6 patient assignments.

accomplishments.title: Falls prevention pilot
accomplishments.problem: Unit had frequent patient falls, especially at night with confused elderly patients.
accomplishments.actions: Joined the falls committee, piloted hourly purposeful rounding and bed-alarm checks on night shift.
accomplishments.results: Unit falls dropped from 11 in 2015 to 5 in 2016 (unit-wide effort, she was one of 4 pilot nurses).

accomplishments.title: Rapid response recognition
accomplishments.problem: Deteriorating telemetry patients were sometimes identified late.
accomplishments.actions: Completed the hospital's early warning score training and became a go-to nurse for escalating to the rapid response team.
accomplishments.results: Recognized by unit manager with a DAISY Award nomination in 2016 for early recognition of a patient's sepsis. Qualitative only.

accomplishments.title: Telemetry rhythm interpretation
accomplishments.problem: Unit monitored up to 32 telemetry patients with a centralized monitor tech.
accomplishments.actions: Completed basic and 12-lead dysrhythmia course; interpreted rhythms and escalated to providers.
accomplishments.results: Scope: cared for 5-6 patients per shift, all on continuous telemetry.

accomplishments.title: PCT support on med-surg while in nursing school
accomplishments.problem: Unit needed reliable part-time support staff.
accomplishments.actions: Performed vital signs, ADLs, point-of-care glucose, ambulation, and EKG lead placement for up to 12 patients per shift.
accomplishments.results: Hired as RN on the same hospital system after graduation.

Charge nurse / staffing and patient assignments
